title: After Games, What?
setting: A long-postponed coffee. Vikram and Sana have been close since university, through a lot of old patterns - a few real fights, more unreal ones. Tonight feels different before either of them says anything.

L1.line: I don't know why I even bother trying with people. Everyone always lets me down eventually.
cues: sets Vikram up as either rescuer or exception
L1.question: What is Sana actually opening with here?

options.text: A plain statement of fact - she's just naming something true.
options.feedback: If it were just a fact, it wouldn't need to be this broad. "Everyone always" is doing work here - it's inviting a reaction, not reporting data.

options.text: A Victim-flavored opener - the real move is testing whether Vikram will rush to be the exception, or push back and prove her right.
options.feedback: Right. Reassuring her too fast makes Vikram the Rescuer; arguing makes him the Persecutor she expected. Either one keeps this a game instead of a conversation.

options.text: A sincere, specific request for comfort.
options.feedback: There's no specific ask here - that absence is exactly the tell that this is an opener, not yet a real request.

L1.lesson: Naming what an opener is doing, without taking it personally and without rushing to fix it, is the precondition for everything that follows - six turns of staying out of Rescuer, Persecutor, and withdrawal, starting now.

L2.intro: Six turns. Sana keeps offering old openings; Vikram has to find something real each time without rescuing, persecuting, or pulling away.

beats.line: I don't know why I even bother trying with people. Everyone always lets me down eventually.

options.text: That sounds lonely. What actually happened today?
options.outcome: She exhales. "...Someone I was counting on bailed on me, again. It's not really about you." The opener relaxes into an actual story.
options.lesson: Asking what actually happened, instead of either reassuring or correcting the blanket claim, is the Adult move that turns an opener into a real conversation.

options.text: You've got me, at least.
options.outcome: "...Yeah. Thanks." Nice, but vague - the actual story never comes out.
options.lesson: Warm, but it answers the feeling behind the opener without ever asking what happened - a mild Rescue, comforting instead of curious.

options.text: You're right, people suck. I'm always here for you no matter what.
options.outcome: Sana settles back, satisfied. "...Yeah. At least I have you." The Victim role locks in.
options.lesson: Agreeing with the "everyone" and installing yourself as the exception is a full Rescue - it feels supportive, and it's exactly what keeps her in the Victim seat.

options.text: That's not really true, you do this every time.
options.outcome: Sana's jaw tightens. "...Wow. Even you." She leans back, vindicated in a different way.
options.lesson: Correcting her confirms the exact accusation the opener was fishing for - Persecutor and Rescuer are two faces of the same unresolved resentment, and this is the Persecutor face.

beats.line: I probably shouldn't have told you that - you're going to think less of me now.
cues: testing reaction to her own admission

options.text: I don't think less of you. I think you've had a rough stretch.
options.outcome: She exhales properly this time. "...Okay. Thank you."
options.lesson: Specific and genuine beats generic reassurance - naming what's actually true (a rough stretch) instead of a blanket "of course not" is what makes this land as real.

options.text: No, of course not...
options.outcome: Trails off, a little flat. Sana looks at him, unconvinced. "...Okay."
options.lesson: Technically the right words, delivered on autopilot - this is reassurance without weight behind it, and she can tell.

options.text: Anyway, how's work going?
options.outcome: Sana blinks. "...Yeah. Fine, I guess." She goes quiet for the rest of the coffee order.
options.lesson: Changing the subject is withdrawal - the third trap alongside rescuing and persecuting. It feels safe, but it closes the exchange just as surely as an argument would.

options.text: Why would you think I'd judge you for that?
options.outcome: "...Sorry, forget it." She retreats, a little stung by the sharpness.
options.lesson: The words defend her, but the tone persecutes - a sharp "why would you think that" lands as pushback, not reassurance.

beats.line: I keep trying to fix things with my sister but nothing works. What would you do?

options.text: What have you already tried?
options.outcome: She lists three things, actually reflecting out loud as she goes. "...huh, I haven't tried just asking her what she needs."
options.lesson: Turning the request back rather than supplying an answer sidesteps the Yes-But trap entirely and lets her find her own next move.

options.text: That's a really hard one.
options.outcome: "Yeah, it is." Sympathetic, and the conversation stalls there.
options.lesson: Sympathy is kind but doesn't move anything - no bait is offered, but nothing opens up either.

options.text: Why don't you just call her and apologize first?
options.outcome: "Yeah, but she never picks up when I call." Classic Yes-But, right on schedule.
options.lesson: Supplying the advice she asked for still walks into the trap - the game's shape doesn't require ill intent from Vikram, just an offered answer to shoot down.

beats.line: You always say you'll be there, but you weren't there when my dad was in the hospital.
cues: old resentment surfacing, real this time

options.text: You're right, I wasn't, and that must have really hurt. I'm sorry - and I'm here now.
options.outcome: Sana's eyes well up. "...Yeah. It did." A real, unguarded moment, no defense, no groveling.
options.lesson: Taking the accusation seriously without over-apologizing or arguing is the harder middle path - accountability without collapsing into one-down and without defending yourself out of it.

options.text: I'm so sorry, I'm honestly the worst friend, I'll make it up to you forever.
options.outcome: "...Okay, it's not that big a deal, I guess." Sana ends up comforting him instead.
options.lesson: Over-apologizing flips the dynamic into a different Rescue - now Sana has to manage Vikram's guilt, which quietly erases the thing she was actually trying to say.

options.text: I was dealing with my own stuff too, you know.
options.outcome: "...Right. Of course you were." Flat, closed off.
options.lesson: A defensive counter-justification, even a true one, lands as Persecution right now - it answers the accusation instead of the hurt underneath it.

beats.line: ...Thanks for not running from that. I bet you're sick of hearing about my problems, though.
cues: genuine thanks, then an old self-deprecating reflex right after

options.text: Not even a little. I like that you tell me real things.
options.outcome: She actually smiles, unguarded. "...Okay. Good."
options.lesson: Matching her candor instead of brushing it off keeps this a genuine exchange - naming what you actually value, not just denying the self-deprecation.

options.text: No, no, it's totally fine!
options.outcome: Quick, a little automatic. "...Okay." The moment passes without quite landing.
options.lesson: Fast reassurance, while not wrong, is slightly dismissive - it closes the topic rather than actually meeting it.

options.text: Maybe we should talk about something lighter.
options.outcome: Sana nods. "...Sure." Something in her goes quiet for the rest of the conversation.
options.lesson: Suggesting a lighter topic is withdrawal again, right near the end - stepping back from real contact feels gentler than it is, but it's the same trap.

beats.line: I don't think I've ever just... talked like this with anyone without it turning into a thing. Is this what it's supposed to feel like?

options.text: Yeah. No roles, no score-keeping - just this. I'm glad we're here.
options.outcome: Sana laughs, a real one. "...Yeah. Me too." Nothing more needs to be said.
options.lesson: This is Berne's answer to "after games, what?" - not a bigger insight or a new plan, just candid, game-free contact sustained long enough to be felt. That's what intimacy is: not a reward for surviving the games, but the thing itself.

options.text: Ha, I guess we're both growing up.
options.outcome: Sana smiles, but something a little real in the moment gets deflected by the joke.
options.lesson: Humor is a gentle way to hold a tender moment, but here it slightly undercuts the realness she just named - a small retreat from candor right at the finish line.

options.text: You just need to keep doing exactly what we did today and you'll be fine.
options.outcome: Sana's face closes slightly. "...Right. Yeah." The warmth cools.
options.lesson: Turning the moment into advice for her future slides back into a Rescue at the very last second - after six turns of staying present, the final move still has to resist fixing her.

fields.label: In under 120 words: write your own honest answer to Berne's closing question, "after games, what?" Use one real or imagined moment where you chose candor over a game.
In under 40 words: name one game you personally fall into most often, and what the antithesis would look like for you.
